key_insight: Higher-order QMC Galerkin FEM yields error bounds for affine-parametric reaction–diffusion problems that remain robust as the perturbation parameter becomes small and the parameter dimension grows.
engineering_relevance: The analysis supports reliable uncertainty quantification for reaction–diffusion simulations with sharp boundary layers and many uncertain reaction-coefficient inputs.
method: Establish perturbation-uniform stability and mixed-parametric regularity in a weighted energy norm.
Combine dimension truncation and higher-order QMC integration with robust finite element approximation.
Verify the spatial approximation property using piecewise affine elements on one-dimensional Shishkin meshes.
evidence_signal: Theoretical error estimates and numerical experiments support the predicted robustness and convergence rates, with the finite element approximation property verified for a one-dimensional model.
watch_item: The general fully discrete guarantee assumes a perturbation-robust finite element approximation property; its verification here is limited to a one-dimensional model.
paper_title: Higher-Order QMC Galerkin FEM for Singular Perturbation: Reaction-Diffusion with Affine-Parametric Reaction
